verdict.rationale: LobeHub's own marketing describes multi-agent teams: automatic team formation that assembles agents for a task, multiple agents sharing context on Pages, and a coordinator that 'dispatched 50 agents' against open issues. That is a first-party claim of agents working together and in parallel. However, all of it is marketing-level copy, with no usage docs on how work is split, delegated or run in parallel, and no hands-on corroboration. missing for 10: documented subagent/delegation mechanics, explicit parallel-execution docs, an agent-to-agent protocol, independent or hands-on verification.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, agents can work together — subagents, swarms, or an agent-to-agent protocol that splits and parallelizes real work

citations.quote: Auto team formation: The system assembles the right Agents for the task.
Write and refine Pages with multiple Agents, all in one place with shared Context.
I had 500 open issues. My CAO dispatched 50 agents. I went to bed.
Anyone can effortlessly build and team up with agent coworkers to deliver complex, systematic work
It hires, schedules, reports on your entire AI team.
